steps.say: Turnloom is for group conversations where someone needs more time to write what they want to say. It keeps your place on the exact statement you mean to answer.
We will start the demo. It has four made-up people deciding where their reading circle should meet.
Each person gets their own invitation. We open the one for Mira.
Sam says the garden gate is sometimes locked. Mira wants to answer that, but not yet. So she keeps a place on Sam's statement.
The workspace now shows that exact statement. Mira chooses what kind of reply this is. Here it is a question, and she keeps the place open.
She writes her words in private. Nobody else can see this draft.

type: Could we ask the librarian whether the gate can stay open for our first meeting? If it cannot, a bench by the front path would help us sit together.

steps.say: She saves the draft, then marks herself ready. Ready means she is available. Her words stay private.
Meanwhile the group moves on. The conversation changes from where we meet to when we meet.
Mira's place stays on Sam's statement. The topic changed, but the link did not.

Now Mira asks for an optional suggestion. The server sends Nemotron, a model from NVIDIA running on Nebius Token Factory, only Sam's statement, the current topic and recent public statements. Her draft is never sent.

The suggestion appears as a separate note. The server accepts it only if it cites Sam's statement, and only if her draft and the conversation have not changed since she asked. Nothing is shared from it.
Mira ignores it. Her words stay exactly as they were.
When she is ready, she brings the original point back. Only a neutral reference to Sam's statement is shared, not her words.
Before anything is shared, she reviews the exact words. Then she chooses to share them as herself.
She shares them. Her contribution now sits next to the point it answers.
Turnloom keeps your words yours, and keeps them connected to the point you meant.
